name: Titanium.Filesystem.File
summary: Object representing a path to a file or directory in the device's persistent storage.
description:
Use the [Titanium.Filesystem.getFile](api:Titanium.Filesystem#getFile) method to get a handle to a `File` object,
which represents a given path.  There does not need to be an existing file or directory
does not need to exist before `getFile` is called. If the file doesn't exist, and
the file path identifies a file in a writable directory, writing to the file
creates the file implicitly.

See [Titanium.Filesystem](api:Titanium.Filesystem) for constants identifying commonly-used device directories.

Use the [exists](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#exists) method to test whether the file exists.

A file object can point to an ordinary file, a directory or a symbolic link.
Use [createDirectory](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#createDirectory) to create a directory.
Use the [getDirectoryListing](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#getDirectoryListing) method to
retrieve a list of the directory's contents.

The `File` object doesn't provide methods for random access into the file.
The `read` method reads the file's entire contents into a `Blob` object.
The `write` method can either overwrite the entire file or append to an
existing file.

For random access to a file, such as accessing a small portion of a larger file,
you can open a file as a [FileStream](api:Titanium.Filesystem.FileStream) object. Use the
[open](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#open) method to get a `FileStream` for an
existing `File` object, or use the [Titanium.Filesystem.openStream](api:Titanium.Filesystem#openStream) method
to get a `FileStream` directly without calling `getFile` first.

The [Titanium.Filesystem](api:Titanium.Filesystem) module defines a number of properties and methods related to
filesystem access, including properties that specify paths for application-specific
directories, and methods for creating temporary files and directories.

On Android, files may be stored on external storage (that is, removable media such as
SD Cards).

Note that once created with `getFile`, the path associated with a file object is
immutable. If you move the underlying file using [move](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#move)
or [rename](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#rename), you can no longer access it with the
original `File` object. You must use `getFile` to get a handle to the new path.

#### Resource Files

The `Resources` directory and all the files in it are read-only. On Android, resource
files are stored in the resource bundle and do not have all of the properties of
normal files. In particular, they do not have creation or modification timestamps.

properties.name: executable
properties.description: On iOS, this property exists but is always `false`.

properties.name: hidden
properties.summary: Set to `true` if the file is hidden.
properties.description: On iOS, this property exists but is always `false`.

properties.name: nativePath
properties.summary: Native path associated with this file object, as a file URL.
properties.description:
On iOS, use the [resolve](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#resolve)
method to obtain a plain file path for use with native modules.

properties.name: parent
properties.summary: A `File` object representing the parent directory of the file identified by this object.
properties.description:
iOS platform-note: Prior to Titanium SDK 7.0.0, this method returned the
path of the parent directory as a String. Since Titanium SDK 7.0.0 it
returns a [Titanium.Filesystem.File](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File) reference for parity wih Android and Windows.

properties.name: readonly
properties.summary: `true` if the file identified by this object is read-only.

properties.name: remoteBackup
properties.summary: Value indicating whether or not to back up to a cloud service.
properties.description:
Some apps may be rejected by Apple for backing up specific files; if this
is the case, ensure that this value is set to `false` for them. This
value should only need to be set once by your app, but setting it
multiple times will not cause problems. For files distributed with your
app, this will need to be set on boot. This flag will only affect iOS
versions 5.0.1 and later, but is safe to set on earlier versions.

Note that setting this property to `false` will also prevent the
file identified by this object from being backed up to iCloud.

properties.name: size
properties.summary: Size, in bytes, of the file identified by this object.

properties.name: symbolicLink
properties.summary: `true` if the file identified by this object is a symbolic link.

properties.name: writable
properties.summary: `true` if the file identified by this object is writable.

methods.name: append
methods.summary: Appends data to the file identified by this file object.
methods.description:
Data to append can be specified as a String, `Blob`, or `File`.

If the `data` argument is a `File` object, the file's contents
are appended to this file.

Returns `true` if the operation succeeds.

methods.name: copy
methods.summary: Copies the file identified by this file object to a new path.

methods.name: createdAt
methods.summary: Returns the creation Date for the file identified by this file object.
methods.description:
On Android, returns a Date whose `getTime()` value is 0 for resource files.

**Important**: When developing for the Apple ecosystem, using this API requires the `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp`
property set in the privacy manifest that was introduced in iOS 17. You can learn more about it [here](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/privacy_manifest_files/describing_use_of_required_reason_api).

methods.name: createDirectory
methods.summary: Creates a directory at the path identified by this file object.
methods.description: Returns `true` if the directory was created successfully.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.summary:
Toggles whether to recursively create the directory structure (like mkdir -p).
Pass `false` to avoid recursively creating the directory.
Defaults to true on SDK 7.3.0+, defaults to false on older SDK versions.

methods.name: createFile
methods.summary: Creates a file at the path identified by this file object.
methods.description:
Note that if you write to a file that doesn't exist, the file is created automatically,
so it is not necessary to call this method unless you want to explicitly create the file
(for example, to create an empty file).

Returns `true` if the file was created successfully. Returns `false` if the
file already exists, or if the file couldn't be created for some other reason.

methods.name: createTimestamp
methods.summary: Returns the creation timestamp for the file identified by this file object.
methods.description: On Android, returns 0 for resource files.

methods.name: deleteDirectory
methods.summary: Deletes the directory identified by this file object.
methods.description:
Returns `true` if the operation was successful. Does nothing if the file
object does not identify a directory.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.summary: Pass `true` to recursively delete any directory contents.

methods.name: deleteFile
methods.summary: Deletes the file identified by this file object.
methods.description: Returns `true` if the operation was successful.

methods.name: exists
methods.summary: Returns `true` if the file or directory identified by this file object exists on the device.

methods.name: extension
methods.summary: Returns the extension for the file identified by this file object.

methods.name: getDirectoryListing
methods.summary:
Returns a listing of the directory identified by this file object, or `null`
if this object doesn't identify a directory.

methods.name: getParent
methods.summary:
Returns the path of the parent directory holding the file identified by this
file object, as a String (deprecated) **or** as a `File` object.
methods.description:
Prior to Titanium SDK 7.0.0, on iOS this method returned the path of the parent
directory as a String. Since Titanium SDK 7.0.0, this method has been deprecated
in favor of the [parent](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#parent) property and will return
a [File](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File) reference in the future as well.

deprecated.notes:
Use the [Titanium.Filesystem.File.parent](Titanium.Filesystem.File.parent) property to receive a `File`
reference instead. If you wish to receive the path, use the `nativePath`
property of that reference instead.

returns.summary: Returns a String on iOS, a `Titanium.Filesystem.File` on Android

methods.name: getProtectionKey
methods.summary:
Returns the protection key value of this file object.
Returns `null` if there's an error.

methods.name: isDirectory
methods.summary: Returns `true` if this file object represents a directory.

methods.name: isFile
methods.summary: Returns `true` if this file object represents an ordinary file.

methods.name: modificationTimestamp
methods.summary: Returns the last modification time for this file.
methods.description: On Android, returns 0 for resource files.

methods.name: modifiedAt
methods.summary: Returns the last modification Date for the file identified by this file object.
methods.description:
On Android, returns a Date whose `getTime()` value is 0 for resource files.

**Important**: When developing for the Apple ecosystem, using this API requires the `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp`
property set in the privacy manifest that was introduced in iOS 17. You can learn more about it [here](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/privacy_manifest_files/describing_use_of_required_reason_api).

methods.name: move
methods.summary: Moves the file identified by this file object to another path.
methods.description:
Note that this method moves the stored file, but doesn't update this
file object to point to the new path. To access the file after moving it,
you must call [getFile](api:Titanium.Filesystem#getFile) using the destination
path to obtain a new file handle.

methods.name: open
methods.summary: Opens the file identified by this file object for random access.
methods.description:
You can open the file for reading, writing, or appending by specifying one of the
`MODE` constants from [Titanium.Filesystem](api:Titanium.Filesystem):
[MODE_READ](api:Titanium.Filesystem#MODE_READ), [MODE_WRITE](api:Titanium.Filesystem#MODE_WRITE),
or [MODE_APPEND](api:Titanium.Filesystem#MODE_APPEND).

The `FileStream` object returned by this call can be used to read from, write to, or
append to the file, depending on what mode the file is opened in.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.summary: Mode to open the file in: `MODE_READ`, `MODE_WRITE`, or `MODE_APPEND`.

methods.name: read
methods.summary: Returns the contents of the file identified by this file object as a `Blob`.

methods.name: rename
methods.summary: Renames the file identified by this file object.
methods.description:
Returns `true` if the file was successfully renamed.

Fails if the destination is in a different directory than the current file.
Use [move](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#move) to move a file to a different directory.

Note that this method renames the stored file, but doesn't update this
file object to point to the new path. To access the file after renaming it,
you must call [getFile](api:Titanium.Filesystem#getFile) using the destination
path to obtain a new file handle.

methods.name: resolve
methods.summary: Returns the fully-resolved native path associated with this file object.
methods.description:
On iOS, the path returned by this method is a plain file path, not a URL. It is suitable
for use in native modules that need to access the file using native APIs.

On Android, the return value of `resolve` is a `file://` URL, identical to the
[nativePath](api:Titanium.Filesystem.File#nativePath) property.

methods.name: setProtectionKey
methods.summary: Sets the protection key as an attribute to the file identified by this file object.
methods.description: Returns `true` if successfully set. Returns `false` if failed.

methods.name: spaceAvailable
methods.summary: Returns the amount of free space available on the device where the file identified by this file object is stored.
methods.description:
Free space is returned in bytes.

**Important**: When developing for the Apple ecosystem, using this API requires the `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace`
property set in the privacy manifest that was introduced in iOS 17. You can learn more about it [here](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/privacy_manifest_files/describing_use_of_required_reason_api).

methods.name: write
methods.summary: Writes the specified data to the file identified by this file object.
methods.description:
If the `append` parameter is `false` or not specified, any existing data in
the file is overwritten.

If `append` is `true`, the specified data is appended to the end of the file.

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: Data to write, as a String, `Blob` or `File` object.

parameters.name: append
parameters.summary: If `true`, append the data to the end of the file.
